commit.message: MCP server: typed, checked actions with outcomes and dry-run prices; schema, catalog, state, results and ui tools

Keep route-server networks on the route server (#265)

With an Open policy and the route server on, the peering desk still picked
networks the route server already reached and stored them as bilateral
sessions. It now skips a request from a network ixSessions() already has,
after drawing its random numbers, so the desk's draws stay as they were.

The changed peer list still moves seeded games a little: the Mid-Atlantic
scenario's floor goes from day 40 to 30 (main wins on days 34-58 across
seeds), and the past week 2026-W44 is regenerated as rev 3.

Let the intern light new fiber with the biggest optic (#262)

The optics order gets an Optics setting: most Gbps per dollar (the old
behaviour, still the default) or the biggest optic on new fiber, the most
Gbps per channel that fits the budget. It is still an intern: once a fiber
is lit it keeps adding what is in there and never swaps optics or line
systems. X.can() takes a quiet flag so asking about an unaffordable optic
is not logged as the budget running out.

Add Best Effort, a soft mode, and quiet notifications

A fourth Normal preset, gentler than Change Freeze: calm chaos (so no DDoS
and no chaos monkey), quick builds and no market, plus four new rules that
only it softens: sea cuts mend on their own clock without cable ships, no
conference season, a five-year Ministry of Tubes rescue loan instead of
game over, and customers who sour half as fast. The new rules are written
into S.rules only when they differ from the classic game, so older networks'
rules stay byte for byte what they were.

Quiet notifications is a new setting for every mode, on by default in Best
Effort: toasts the day itself raises pop up only for trouble and milestones,
the rest goes to the NOC log; what a click says still shows. Best Effort
badges count as Freeze-dried. The preset picker is four wide, two by two on
a phone in portrait.

commit.message:
Port Hedland, Townsville and Alice Springs; the wet season up north (closes #255)

Three cities in the gaps of northern Australia, Telstraya everywhere, Hocus
Pocus in Port Hedland and Townsville, Aussie Boyband in Townsville. Port
Hedland lands the No Worries Cable System up to Darwin (the real NWCS) and a
Port Hedland-Singapore pair on the Darwin Award Cable (the DJSC interconnect
onto the ASC). Alice Springs has no cable and its only facility is an old
telegraph station.

Cities in the tropical north (Darwin, Port Hedland, Townsville) are wet: from
November to April a cut on land there takes twice as long to reach, with its
own message. The real DigiCo, iseek, NEXTDC, NWCS and DJSC names go on the
blocklist.

Pay to hurry the permits and factory of your own subsea cable (closes #258)

Before laying starts, seaRush buys 30 days a step (or all of them at once)

leadDays), then the lay ships still need their time at sea, which a second
ship still halves. 6,000 km: from 600 days of prep to 132 for about $13M.

+## Acting
+
+`act` checks the arguments against `schema` first: a wrong id or value is an error that says what would fit, and
+nothing runs. The action then runs as the game runs it, with what a player would type and pick filled in: a rename,
+a RouteScript, a custom metric, the route and size of a link, the source and line system of dark fiber, the design
+of a cable, the POPs to close. Confirmations are given, so `rmLink` removes the link in one call. The result says
+what happened:
+
+| `outcome` | Meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `applied` | Something changed. `charged` is what the game's money gate took; `cashChange` also counts goal rewards |
+| `rejected` | The game said no; `toasts` has its words |
+| `no_effect` | Nothing changed and nothing was said: usually a wrong id or a precondition |
+| `shown` | A view or a draft: only the screen changed |
+| `decision` | A window asks a question (a De-Kicks quote, a retention offer). Answer with one of `decision.options` or `closeModal`; other game commands wait until then |
+| `quote` | With `dryRun`: `{setup, monthly, days, blocked}`, priced with the game's own helpers. Nothing happens, and no dice are rolled |
+| `stopped` | The network is bankrupt |
+
+`click` presses a button as a player's click does, with the button's own arguments, so a confirmation arms first
+and windows step on as they do in the game. Lists the game acts on when they change are listed with their options
+and clicked with a value. Neither tool reaches files, save slots, settings, the title screen or the game speed: time
+moves only with `advance`. There is no tool that evaluates code in the page.

 1. `load_save` with the save attached to the issue.
-2. `status` and `hot_spots` for the picture, `traceroute` and `peering_check` for one network's traffic.
+2. `status` and `hot_spots` for the picture, `traceroute` and `peering_check` for one network's traffic, `state`
+   and `results` for the numbers behind them.
 3. `advance` a few days and read `timing.slowestDays` for lag, or the log for what went wrong.
 
 ## Code
 
 - `scripts/mcp.js`: the stdio transport (JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line) and the protocol methods.
 - `scripts/lib/mcp-game.js`: the session (one game page) and the tool list with input schemas.
+- `scripts/lib/mcp-commands.js`: runs inside the page: every action's class, arguments, domains, price and
+  description, and the `state`/`results` field reference.
